description: ECG recognition of acute myocardial infarction and STEMI patterns
overview: This module covers the ECG changes associated with acute myocardial infarction, including ST elevation, Q waves, and regional wall motion abnormalities.
objectives: Understand the evolution of MI changes
Learn emergency management of acute MI

slides.title: ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
slides.content: STEMI: ST elevation ≥1mm in 2 contiguous leads, new Q waves, T wave inversion. Requires immediate reperfusion therapy. Time is muscle - door-to-balloon time <90 minutes.

slides.title: Regional Wall Motion Abnormalities
slides.content: Different leads correspond to different heart regions: anterior (V1-V4), lateral (I, aVL, V5-V6), inferior (II, III, aVF), posterior (V7-V9). Localize the infarction by affected leads.

quiz.question: Which leads are most important for diagnosing anterior wall MI?
quiz.explanation: V3-V4 are most important for diagnosing anterior wall myocardial infarction.

slides.title: Evolution of MI Changes
slides.content: MI evolution: hyperacute T waves → ST elevation → Q waves → T wave inversion → normalization. Timeline varies but changes may persist for months to years.

quiz.question: What is the first ECG change in acute MI?
quiz.explanation: Hyperacute T waves are often the first ECG change in acute myocardial infarction.

slides.title: Emergency Management
slides.content: Emergency management: immediate ECG, oxygen, aspirin, nitroglycerin (if no contraindications), pain control, primary PCI or thrombolytics. Activate cardiac catheterization lab immediately.

quiz.question: What is the target door-to-balloon time for STEMI?
quiz.explanation: The target door-to-balloon time for STEMI is less than 90 minutes for optimal outcomes.
